name: ESS Sabre
_note: Never bit-exact, in PCM or DSD: everything goes through its internal DSP. Author: "ESS is out since it's always through DSP". Consequence: not correctable. That is the ONLY consequence - it does not follow that the part re-converts DSD to PCM, and the same author recommends DSD output to ESS parts. See dsd_reconverted_to_pcm.
_dsd_reconverted_to_pcm: Not established by the family note, which concludes only that nothing is bit-exact. A recognised expert recommends DSD output to ESS parts by name — fifth-order modulation before the ES9039 — which he would not do for a converter that undoes the work. So: not re-converted, and not correctable. The citation is in the record's source field and should be checkable; where it is not yet, that is a gap to close rather than a claim to keep.
_replaced_a_device_record: Until 2026-11-24 a DEVICE record stood beside this family - devices/unknown/ess-generique - whose own source called it « Fallback entry, not a measured device. Chip-level facts only. » Its identity was brand "unknown", model "unknown", shared with two other records, and it asserted for every converter on this silicon the four fields _what_the_implementation_fixes says the silicon does NOT fix. It is gone, and nothing moved here: `family` was self-referential, `analog_filter` cannot live on a chip by this catalogue's own rule, and `correctable` is computed from dsd_direct on all 27 records. A chip's defaults belong in a chip family; they do not need a device to carry them.
